title: Supervisory Judgement and Professional Practice
summary: A ten-module programme on forming, documenting and defending supervisory judgements, and turning them into clear findings, letters and interventions.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors to form, document and defend sound supervisory judgements, and to turn them into clear findings, letters and interventions that firms act on and that stand up to internal and external scrutiny.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip supervisors with the professional disciplines that turn information into well-reasoned, proportionate and defensible supervisory judgements. Participants leave able to weigh evidence with scepticism, recognise bias, communicate findings clearly in writing and in person, and escalate and act with integrity and independence.
sections.What It Covers: The nature of supervisory judgement, evidence and professional scepticism, cognitive bias, proportionality and prioritisation, meetings with boards and senior management, difficult conversations, report and letter writing, findings and risk mitigation programmes, escalation, and ethics and independence.
Intended Audience: Supervisors and senior supervisors responsible for risk assessments, firm engagement and supervisory findings
Team leaders and managers who review, challenge and sign off supervisory judgements and correspondence
Staff in enforcement, authorisation and policy functions who rely on, or contribute to, supervisory conclusions
Learning Objectives: Explain what supervisory judgement is and why it must be exercised under uncertainty
Evaluate evidence with professional scepticism and recognise the biases that distort decisions
Apply proportionality to prioritise risks and select the right supervisory response
Communicate findings clearly and firmly in meetings, reports and supervisory letters
Design findings and risk mitigation programmes that are specific, measurable and followed up
Act with integrity and independence, and escalate and defend judgements under challenge
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short briefings with case studies, drafting exercises and role-play, and can be selected or tailored to the authority's supervisory approach.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervising regulated firms is helpful. The programme is suitable for both newer and experienced supervisors.
Core Reading: IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)
Daniel Kahneman, Olivier Sibony and Cass R. Sunstein, Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgment (2021)
Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011)

modules.title: The Nature of Supervisory Judgement
modules.summary: Why supervision depends on judgement rather than rule-checking alone, where uncertainty comes from, and what accountability for a judgement requires of the individual supervisor and the authority.
objectives: Explain the role of judgement in risk-based, forward-looking supervision
Identify the main sources of uncertainty in supervisory decisions
Distinguish judgement from discretion and describe what accountability requires
syllabus: From compliance checking to judgement-led supervision
Sources of uncertainty: incomplete information, evolving risk and ambiguous rules
The cost of over- and under-cautious judgements
Judgement, discretion and the supervisor's accountability

modules.title: Evidence, Professional Scepticism and Challenge
modules.summary: How supervisors gather and weigh evidence, test management's assertions rather than accept them, and decide when the evidence is sufficient to support a conclusion.
objectives: Assess the reliability, relevance and sufficiency of supervisory evidence
Apply professional scepticism to firms' assertions and management information
Challenge firms constructively while keeping an open mind
syllabus: Types of evidence: documents, data, interviews and observation
Corroboration, triangulation and testing assertions
Red flags: comfort without evidence and over-polished narratives
When is enough evidence enough to conclude

modules.title: Cognitive Bias and Structured Decision-Making
modules.summary: The biases that affect experienced and new supervisors alike, how they distort risk assessment, and the structured frameworks and safeguards that make judgements more consistent.
objectives: Identify common cognitive biases in supervisory decisions
Apply structured judgement frameworks to reduce inconsistency
Evaluate the safeguards that counter individual and group bias
syllabus: Confirmation bias, anchoring, groupthink, optimism and hindsight bias
How bias distorts risk ratings and relationship supervision
Structured frameworks, pre-mortems and devil's advocate techniques
Panels, peer review and calibration as structural safeguards

modules.title: Proportionality and Risk-Based Prioritisation
modules.summary: How to match supervisory effort and response to the size of the risk, prioritise issues across a portfolio, and select the right tool from the supervisory toolkit.
objectives: Apply proportionality to the scale, nature and impact of a firm's risks
Prioritise issues using impact, probability and supervisory objectives
Select a supervisory tool or intervention that fits the risk
syllabus: Proportionality in principle and in practice
Impact and probability: prioritising across firms and issues
The supervisory toolkit: from dialogue to formal powers
Avoiding both regulatory overreach and supervisory forbearance

modules.title: Meetings with Boards and Senior Management
modules.summary: How to plan and run effective supervisory meetings with chairs, directors and senior managers, set the agenda, test understanding and leave with clear outcomes.
objectives: Plan a supervisory meeting with clear objectives and lines of enquiry
Engage senior individuals with authority, courtesy and challenge
Record outcomes and agree next steps that can be followed up
syllabus: Purpose of meetings: risk assessment, findings and relationship building
Preparation: briefing packs, agendas and question sets
Chairing and steering the meeting while testing understanding
Meeting notes, actions and confirming outcomes in writing

modules.title: Difficult Conversations and Managing Pushback
modules.summary: How to deliver adverse findings and unwelcome decisions clearly and constructively, handle defensive or aggressive reactions, and stay firm without becoming inflexible.
objectives: Explain why firms react defensively to adverse findings
Apply techniques for delivering difficult messages clearly
Manage pushback while protecting credibility for future engagement
syllabus: Types of difficult supervisory conversation and how to prepare
Structuring the delivery of an adverse finding
Handling challenge, lobbying and appeals to seniority
Role-play: delivering a finding to a senior manager

modules.title: Writing Supervisory Reports and Letters
modules.summary: How to write clear, authoritative and defensible reports, internal papers and supervisory letters that set out findings, expectations and next steps for the right audience.
objectives: Apply the principles of clear, authoritative regulatory writing
Structure internal papers and supervisory letters for decision and action
Evaluate drafts for clarity, tone and legal and reputational risk
syllabus: Writing for the reader: decision-makers, boards and firms
Structuring a supervisory letter: findings, expectations and deadlines
Calibrating tone: firmness, fairness and avoiding ambiguity
Drafting exercise: a supervisory letter following a review

modules.title: Findings and Risk Mitigation Programmes
modules.summary: How to turn analysis into well-evidenced findings and a risk mitigation programme with specific, measurable actions, owners and deadlines, and how to track remediation to closure.
objectives: Formulate findings that link evidence, root cause and risk
Design a risk mitigation programme with measurable actions and deadlines
Assess whether remediation is complete, effective and sustained
syllabus: Anatomy of a good finding: issue, evidence, root cause and impact
Designing actions, owners, deadlines and evidence of completion
Tracking remediation and validating closure
Red flags: repeat findings, slippage and cosmetic remediation

modules.title: Escalation, Ethics and Independence
modules.summary: When and how to escalate concerns within the authority, the ethical standards supervisors must uphold, and how to protect independence against capture, conflicts and external pressure.
objectives: Identify the triggers and routes for escalating supervisory concerns
Recognise conflicts of interest, capture and other threats to independence
Apply ethical standards to grey-area situations in supervisory work
syllabus: Escalation triggers, routes and the escalation paper
Regulatory capture, familiarity threats and conflicts of interest
Gifts, hospitality, confidentiality and post-employment considerations
Ethical dilemmas: case discussions from supervisory practice

modules.title: Forming and Defending Judgements: Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a case study in which participants form a judgement on an ambiguous scenario, document it, present it to a review panel and defend it under challenge.
objectives: Formulate a reasoned judgement on an ambiguous supervisory scenario
Document the reasoning so that it is defensible under later scrutiny
Defend a judgement before a panel and respond to challenge
syllabus: Recording the rationale: options considered and reasons for the decision
Hindsight, internal review and external scrutiny of supervisory decisions
Presenting to a review or risk panel
Workshop: form, document and defend a supervisory judgement

related.title: Investigative and Interviewing Skills for Supervisors
related.summary: An eight-module practical programme on planning and conducting supervisory interviews and turning interview evidence into sound findings.

related.title: Core Professional Skills for Regulatory Staff
related.summary: An eight-module practical programme building the core writing, analysis, meeting, challenge, presentation and data skills that regulatory staff need every day.

related.title: Assessing Board Effectiveness
related.summary: An eight-module programme showing supervisors how to assess how a board really works, from papers and decisions to culture and challenge, culminating in case-study interviews.

related.title: Core Supervisory Skills: Business Models, Governance and Risk Governance Panels
related.summary: A three-day workshop taking supervisors from business model analysis through governance interviews to a risk governance panel, using running case studies and role plays.

related.title: Foundations of Financial Regulation and Supervision
related.summary: An eight-module induction for new regulatory staff covering why we regulate, the authority's powers, risk-based supervision and a first supervisory case.

related.title: How Financial Firms Work: Business Models and Financial Statements for Supervisors
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping supervisors understand how financial firms make money, read their accounts and identify capital, liquidity and business model risks.
